metadata.name: Code design
metadata.description: Structure functions, modules, and folders so operations read clearly, computation stays separate from effects, and each feature's code stays together.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, implementing, refactoring, or reviewing function, module, or folder structure.

metadata.name: Concurrency
metadata.description: Keep shared resources safe for concurrent users and honor cancellation and deadlines throughout blocking operations.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, implementing, or reviewing concurrent operations, shared-resource initialization, replacement or cleanup, or blocking operations that support cancellation or deadlines. Common scenarios include parallel HTTP requests, background workers, database reads and writes through connection pools, replacing clients after credential rotation, cache refreshes, retries, and graceful shutdown.

metadata.name: Performance
metadata.description: Improve speed and resource use where measurement shows it matters, without changing behavior.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, implementing, changing, reviewing, or diagnosing code for speed or resource use, such as a slow loop, render, request, or data transformation.

metadata.name: READMEs
metadata.description: Write a README that says what the product does for the reader, gets a new user to a working result, states its limits, and links to the full documentation, with a presentation that matches whether the product is primary or secondary.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, writing, restructuring, or reviewing a repository's README, such as launching a product, preparing a release that changes setup, or moving material between the README and the documentation.

metadata.name: Testing
metadata.description: Spend test effort where bugs are likely and costly, prove each behavior at the lowest layer that can, keep tests independent and focused on observable behavior, cover regressions and boundary cases, and name and run tests for clear feedback.
metadata.whenToRead: When adding or changing behavior, fixing a bug, or writing, running, and reviewing tests.

metadata.name: Go
metadata.description: Write clear, maintainable Go that follows the language's conventions.
metadata.whenToRead: Before planning, writing, or reviewing Go code.

metadata.name: JavaScript
metadata.description: Coordinate asynchronous work, use browser DOM, event, storage, and scheduling APIs, and keep code analyzable by build tools, in JavaScript and TypeScript.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, implementing, changing, or reviewing JavaScript or TypeScript code that runs asynchronous operations, uses browser APIs, or builds dynamic import and file paths.

metadata.name: TypeScript
metadata.description: Design TypeScript types, functions, modules, naming, and tests.
metadata.whenToRead: When planning, implementing, changing, or reviewing TypeScript code.
